1.explanation:
This minimal React app imports the `DataTable` and `TableContainer` components from Carbon. We pass a visible `title` and `description` into `` and spread the props returned from `getTableContainerProps` onto it. Under the hood, `TableContainer` renders its own heading (`

`) and paragraph (`

`) elements for the title/description, but it doesn’t assign IDs to those elements nor set the corresponding `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` on the ``. When you run the app and inspect the DOM (or expose the table list to JAWS), you will see the table has no ARIA relationship to the title/description and the screen reader will announce your column headers (or fall back to an `aria-label`) instead of reading “Table title” and “Table description.” This reproduces the bug scenario described in the report.
1.bug_scenario: When you render a DataTable with a TableContainer that provides a visible title and description (via the `title` and `description` props), TableContainer does not generate or apply any IDs on those elements nor does it wire up the table’s `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby` attributes to point at them. As a result, a screen reader (e.g. JAWS) will not announce the human-readable title/description for the table and instead will fall back to reading column headers as the table’s label (or require using `aria-label` on the Table).
